# Sample output

A complete result set, committed so the tool's output can be read without
building or running anything.

**Generated by `make demo` against the local mock responder.** Nothing here
describes a real timestamp provider. The mock signs in-process, so the
latencies below are the latency of a local signature — around a millisecond,
and meaningless as a capacity figure. What the files *do* show faithfully is
the shape of the output: what is recorded, per stage and per attempt, and how a
verified transaction is distinguished from an HTTP 200.

Reproduce it with:

```sh
make build && make demo
```

## What the run did

`profiles/demo.yaml`, a four-stage rate ladder. 2,800 requests, every one of
them carried through the full RFC 3161 acceptance chain, zero failures.

| Stage | Target | Sent | Verified | Achieved | p95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `functional` | sequential | 50 | 50 | — | 0.60 ms |
| `ramp-50` | 50 TPS | 250 | 250 | 49.99 TPS | 1.64 ms |
| `ramp-100` | 100 TPS | 500 | 500 | 99.98 TPS | 1.32 ms |
| `hold-200` | 200 TPS | 2,000 | 2,000 | 199.99 TPS | 1.21 ms |
| **overall** | | **2,800** | **2,800** | 121.72 TPS | 1.39 ms |

## Files

| File | |
|---|---|
| `report.html` | the executive summary — open this one first |
| `comparison.html` | the side-by-side view `report` builds from one or more runs |
| `summary.json` | every metric, per stage and overall |
| `metadata.json` | run environment and configuration, redacted |
| `timeseries.csv` | per-second throughput, errors and client resource use |
| `errors.csv` | failed attempts with their classification (header only here) |
| `comparison.json`, `comparison.csv` | machine-readable forms of the comparison |
| `requests.head.csv` | the first 50 rows of `requests.csv` |
| `run.head.log` | the first lines of the structured run log |

`requests.csv` and `run.log` are truncated here; a real run writes one row per
attempt — 2,801 lines including the header, in this case — and a full JSON log.

## Three things worth noticing

**Every stage hit its target to within 0.02 %.** That is the open-loop
scheduler doing its job: request *n* is released at `start + n/rate` whatever
request *n-1* is doing. `client_saturation_events` is 0 and `schedule_lag`
stays flat, which is how the report says the *client* was not the constraint.

**The overall achieved rate is lower than any stage's target.** 121.72 TPS is
the rate across the whole run including the pauses between stages — not a sign
of anything failing. Per-stage rates are the ones to read.

**`metadata.json` was written with `--redact-host`**, so `hostname` and
`command_line` are masked and the trust anchor is recorded by filename rather
than by its path on the operator's disk. That flag is what makes a result set
safe to hand to someone outside the organisation.
